questions.question: An administrator wants to open the list of all user records directly from the Unified Navigation filter. What should they type in the filter field?

explanation.correct: In the Unified Navigation filter you can type a table name followed by .list to open that table's list view (for example sys_properties.list). Typing the table name followed by .do opens a form instead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The .do suffix opens a form view for the table (for example sys_user.do opens a new user form), not the list.
There is no 'list:' prefix syntax in the navigation filter; the documented format is name.list.
'.form' is not a documented navigation filter suffix; forms use name.do.

source.excerpt: For a list view, enter the table name in the format name.list

questions.question: By default, filtering in any of the Unified Navigation menus returns results from all menus except one. Which menu is excluded?

explanation.correct: The Unified Navigation documentation states that by default, filtering in any of the menus returns results from all menus except the History menu. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Favorites are included in filter results by default.
The All menu, which lists all menu items and modules, is included in filter results.
The Admin menu is included in filter results by default.

source.excerpt: By default, filtering in any of the menus returns results from all menus, except the History menu.

questions.question: A user is on a page they visit every day and wants to add it to their Favorites menu in Next Experience. What is the quickest way to do this from any page?

options.text: Select the star icon in the contextual app pill
Right-click the browser tab and select Bookmark
Open the History menu and drag the page to the Admin menu
Ask an administrator to add a module to the application menu

explanation.correct: From any page, a user can select the star icon in the contextual app pill to add the page to the Favorites menu. No role is required to add favorites. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/add-favorites-next-experience.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A browser bookmark is not a ServiceNow favorite and does not appear in the Favorites menu.
The History menu shows past activity; dragging items to the Admin menu is not how favorites are created.
Users can add their own favorites without an administrator; no role is required.

source.excerpt: From any page, select the star icon in the contextual app pill. … Role required: none

questions.question: Which Unified Navigation control lets a user select the current application scope and the current update set?

explanation.correct: The Globe menu in the Unified Navigation lets you select the scope of your instance and the scope of your update sets, and you can create an update set from it. Any application scope other than Global displays a red circle icon. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The contextual app pill shows where you are in the instance and lets you favorite the page; it does not change scope or update set.
The History menu lists your recent activity.
The Favorites menu lists items you have marked as favorites.

source.excerpt: Select the scope of your instance and the scope of your update sets.

questions.question: A newly hired fulfiller reports that there is no Workspaces menu in their Unified Navigation header, while a colleague has one. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The user does not have access to any workspace
The user has not pinned the All menu
The user's browser does not support Next Experience
The instance has more than one update set in progress

explanation.correct: The Workspaces menu lists the workspaces you can access and appears only when workspace access is available. If a user has one workspace, its name appears in the header instead. The items in Unified Navigation are determined by user access and admin customizations. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pinning the All menu only keeps that menu open; it does not control whether the Workspaces menu appears.
Menu visibility is driven by user access, not by the browser.
Update sets have no effect on which Unified Navigation menus a user sees.

source.excerpt: The menu appears only when workspace access is available.

questions.question: An agent types a record number such as INC0010023 into the Unified Navigation search field but does not press Enter. What does the search field do?

options.text: It displays a preview of the matching record with an Exact Match tag that opens the record directly
It opens the full search results page grouped by table
It filters the All menu for modules containing that text
It creates a new incident with that number

explanation.correct: If you enter a record number into the Unified Navigation search field without pressing Enter or selecting View results, the search field displays a preview of the record with an Exact Match tag. Selecting the preview goes directly to the record, bypassing the search results page. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-search-next-experience.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The search results page appears only after pressing Enter or selecting View results.
The All menu filter is a separate control from the global search field.
Global search never creates records.

source.excerpt: The search field displays a preview of the record with an Exact Match tag.

questions.question: In Next Experience on Microsoft Windows, which keyboard shortcut displays the keyboard shortcuts available for the page you are viewing?

explanation.correct: Control+/ (Command+/ on macOS) shows the shortcuts for the page you are viewing in a modal. The shortcuts shown are specific to the current screen. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/next-experience-keyboard-shortcuts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Control+Alt+a opens the All menu.
Control+s saves the record.
Shift+Alt+n creates a new record.

source.excerpt: Show the shortcuts for the page that you’re viewing in a modal|Control+/

questions.question: Which Next Experience preference category appears only for users with the admin role?

explanation.correct: The Next Experience Preferences modal includes display, accessibility, debugging, theme, notification, language and region, workspace, and user experience preferences. The debugging preferences appear only for users with the admin role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/set-up-preferences-next-experience.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Display preferences control layout and density for the current user and are available to all users.
Language and region preferences, including time zone and date format, are available to users.
Notification preferences control how users receive notifications and are available to users.

source.excerpt: The debugging preferences only appear for users with the admin role.

questions.question: A user wants to change their own time zone and date format in Next Experience. Which preference category should they use?

explanation.correct: The Language and region preferences let a user define their language, time zone, and date and time formats. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/set-up-preferences-next-experience.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Display preferences control layout, visual density and presentation options.
Accessibility preferences cover needs such as keyboard navigation, contrast and motion.
Workspace preferences customize behavior inside a specific workspace and appear only when a workspace is in focus.

source.excerpt: Define your language, time zone, and date and time formats.

questions.question: An administrator added a new module, but it does not appear in their All menu yet. What does the documentation suggest to get the latest menu items without manually clearing the cache?

options.text: Select the refresh icon in the All menu
Log out and clear the browser history
Run cache.do from the navigation filter
Activate the menu in the Favorites menu

explanation.correct: The All menu lists all menu items and modules in the instance. Selecting its refresh icon obtains the latest menu items without the need to manually clear the cache. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Logging out and clearing browser history is not required; the All menu has its own refresh control.
Flushing the system cache has a performance impact and is unnecessary to refresh the menu.
Favorites cannot activate modules that are not yet showing in the All menu.

source.excerpt: to obtain the latest menu items without the need to manually clear the cache.

questions.question: Which element of the Unified Navigation header provides context for where you are in the instance and includes a star icon to favorite the displayed page?

explanation.correct: The contextual app pill provides the context for where you are in the instance. Select its star icon to favorite the displayed page. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Globe lets you select the application scope and update set.
The Admin menu provides access to admin-specific items.
Show instance tools displays the application scope and current update set in a row beneath the tool icons.

source.excerpt: Provides the context for where you are in the instance. Select the star icon to favorite the displayed page.

questions.question: How does ServiceNow describe the ServiceNow AI Platform in its administration documentation?

options.text: An application platform as a service that automates business processes across the enterprise
An on-premises database server that each customer installs and patches
A desktop productivity suite for editing documents offline
An infrastructure-as-a-service offering for hosting virtual machines

explanation.correct: The documentation describes the ServiceNow AI Platform as an application platform as a service that automates business processes across the enterprise. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/intro-now-platform-landing.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow is delivered as a cloud platform service, not as a database server that customers install.
ServiceNow is not a desktop productivity suite.
ServiceNow provides an application platform, not raw virtual machine hosting.

source.excerpt: The ServiceNow AI Platform is an application platform as a service that automates business processes across the enterprise.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow application is described as a central hub for platform owners and admins to access platform capabilities, discover new applications, and get actionable insights?

explanation.correct: Admin Center is a central hub for platform owners and admins to access platform capabilities, discover new applications, and get intelligent, actionable insights. It gives access to tools such as Application Manager, Security Center, and Subscription Management. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/intro-now-platform-landing.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Portal is a self-service interface for end users.
Schema Map visualizes table relationships.
Update sets capture configuration changes for moving between instances.

source.excerpt: A central hub for platform owners and admins to access platform capabilities, discover new applications, and get intelligent, actionable insights.

questions.question: Which applications can an administrator open directly from the Admin menu in Admin Center? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Admin Center offers access to key admin applications from the Admin menu, including Adoption Blueprints, AI Admin Hub, Application Manager, Security Center, Subscription Management, Configuration Hub, and Upgrade Management. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/admin-center/ac-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Visual Task Boards are a collaboration tool, not one of the Admin Center applications.
Knowledge Base is a self-service application, not listed among the Admin Center applications.
Service Catalog is a self-service application, not listed among the Admin Center applications.

source.excerpt: Application Manager: As an admin, you have the ability to install … Security Center: Use the Security Center application

questions.question: What happens to the target instance when an administrator runs an instance clone?

options.text: Data and configuration from the source instance are copied to the target, overwriting the target
Only update sets are copied, and target data is untouched
The source instance is overwritten with the target's data
The two instances are merged and duplicates are removed

explanation.correct: Clone copies data and configuration from a source instance to a target instance, overwriting the target. Clones are commonly used to reset sub-production instances that have drifted from production, for example before validating upgrades. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/exploring-instance-clone.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A clone copies the database, not only update sets, and it overwrites the target.
The source is copied from, not overwritten.
A clone does not merge instances; it overwrites the target.

source.excerpt: Clone copies data and configuration from a source instance to a target instance, overwriting the target.

questions.question: Which role allows a user to request, cancel, or schedule instance clones?

explanation.correct: Clone administrators with the clone_admin role can request, cancel, or schedule clones. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/exploring-instance-clone.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The itil role is for fulfilling ITSM work, not administering clones.
catalog_admin administers the Service Catalog.
knowledge_admin administers knowledge bases.

source.excerpt: Clone admins with the clone_admin role can request, cancel, or schedule clones.

questions.question: Where does instance clone data come from?

options.text: The most recent daily backup of the source instance
A live replica of the target instance
The update sets committed on the source instance
An export of the source instance's XML files

explanation.correct: Clone data is sourced from the most recent daily backup of the source instance. If there were major recent changes, a new backup is created, and an on-demand backup can be triggered from the Clone Admin Console. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/exploring-instance-clone.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The target is what gets overwritten; the data comes from the source.
Update sets contain configuration changes only, while a clone copies data and configuration.
Clones restore from a backup, not from exported XML files.

source.excerpt: Clone data is sourced from the most recent daily backup of the source instance.

questions.question: An administrator wants to open a new User form directly from the Unified Navigation filter field. What should they enter?

explanation.correct: In the filter field, enter name.do to open a form view, for example sys_user.do. Enter name.list to open a list view, for example sys_properties.list. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: name.list opens a list, not a form.
name.form isn't the documented format.
This isn't a valid table name or format.

source.excerpt: For a form view, enter the table name in the format name.do, for example, sys_user.do.

questions.question: Which Unified Navigation menu shows the history of your activities across the instance?

explanation.correct: The History menu shows the history of your activities across the instance. Favorites holds items you marked as favorites, All lists all menu items and modules, and Workspaces lists the workspaces you can access. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Favorites holds items you marked as favorites.
All lists all menu items and modules.
Workspaces lists the workspaces you can access.

source.excerpt: History of your activities across the instance.
